label: input token a during the original phase
explanation: Token detector for the letter a when it is read as an original (pre-<DEL>) input. Fires on essentially every original-phase a at any position and for any L (dev precision 1.00, recall 0.9997). It does not fire on any other token, on the delimiter, or on a when the model feeds it back during the copy phase (only 36 stray copy-phase activations). Magnitude is highest when a is the first token (t=0, all top examples reach max 2.97) and falls off at later positions (t=8 carries 1.0% of mass but 2.7% of activations). A repeated a (not the first occurrence) also fires, but more weakly: 9.4% of activations and 7.5% of mass.

issues: Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.9997, F1 0.9998, mass recall 0.999996. The predicate has 0 false positives.

There are 32 missed activations on test (36 on dev). They hold 0.0% of the mass and have relative activations of 0.00-0.02. All of them are the fed-back 'a' at step 4 in L=3 sequences that start with 'a' (recall_idx 1). This is a consistent pattern but negligible in size, so it counts as noise.

Every claim checked out on dev. The feature fires only on in_tok 'a' (lift 32.9x), never on <DEL>, and on only 36 copy-phase steps. t=0 holds 15.9% of activations but 20.5% of mass, so it is stronger than average. t=8 holds 2.7% of activations and 1.0% of mass. Repeated 'a' (in_first==0) holds 9.4% of activations and 7.5% of mass. Every activation quartile is covered at 99.9% or more.

One small caveat: the activation rate is about 0.033 at every orig_idx. So the falling share of activations at later t comes mostly from fewer sequences being long enough to reach those positions. The drop in mass share is larger than the drop in count, which fits the claim that activations get weaker at later positions.
